Currently md devices
is unloaded.  This is essentially because the gendisk holds a
reference to the mddev
column2: and the mddev holds a reference to the

column1: gendisk
If we drop the reference from mddev to gendisk
that the mddev is destroyed when the gendisk is destroyed.  However it
is not possible to hook into the gendisk destruction process to enable
this.
So we drop the reference from the gendisk to the mddev and destroy the
gendisk when the mddev gets destroyed.  However this has a
complication.
Between the call
__blkdev_get->get_gendisk->kobj_lookup->md_probe
and the call
__blkdev_get->md_open
there is no obvious way to hold a reference on the mddev any more
unless something is done
column2: it will disappear and gendisk will be

column1: destroyed prematurely.
Also
column2: once we decide to destroy the mddev

column1: moment before the gendisk is unlinked (blk_unregister_region) during
which a new reference to the gendisk can be created.  We need to
ensure that this reference can not be used.  i.e. the ->open must
fail.
So:
1/  in md_probe we set a flag in the mddev (hold_active) which
indicates that the array should be treated as active
though there are no references
This is cleared by md_release when the device is closed if it
is no longer needed.
This ensures that the gendisk will survive between md_probe and
md_open.
2/  In md_open we check if the mddev we expect to open matches
the gendisk that we did open.
If there is a mismatch we return -ERESTARTSYS and modify
__blkdev_get to retry from the top in that case.
In the -ERESTARTSYS sys case we make sure to wait until
the old gendisk (that we succeeded in opening) is really gone so
we loop at most once.
Some udev configurations will always open an md device when it first
appears.   If we allow an md device that was just created by an open
to disappear on an immediate close
column2: then this can race with such udev

column1: configurations and result in an infinite loop the device being opened
and closed
column2: then re-open due to the 'ADD' even from the first open

column1: and then close and so on.
So we make sure an md device
at least until some md 'ioctl' has been made on it.  This means that
all normal usage of md devices will allow them to disappear promptly
when not needed
column2: but the worst that an incorrect usage will do it

column1: cause an inactive md device to be left in existence (it can easily be
removed).
As an array can be stopped by writing to a sysfs attribute
echo clear > /sys/block/mdXXX/md/array_state
we need to use scheduled work for deleting the gendisk and other
kobjects.  This allows us to wait for any pending gendisk deletion to
complete by simply calling flush_scheduled_work().
